text:
max: Heads-up — we need to pick a single approach for trace lifecycles across envs. Prod team wants full-text search + 90d lookback. Finance is worried about cost. thoughts?

anya: do we mean full spans + index for 90d, or just span metadata index? big cost diff.

max: they want full spans searchable (stack traces, annotations) for 90d. suggested fallback: keep full spans hot for 30d then archive compressed for 60d.

raj: hot->archive sounds fine but we need a clear rehydration path for console trace view. rehydration latency matters for SRE during incidents.

sylvia: rehydrate job would be fine if <30s for a single trace. anything longer and console UX breaks. also we need a retention config that ties to service criticality not just env.

anya: agree on service-criticality tiers. proposal sketch: prod-critical: hot 30d full, cold archived compressed 60d (rehydrate on demand). prod-noncritical: hot 7d full, cold 83d compressed. staging/dev: hot 3d full, then delete.

max: can we do attribute-level retention to shave size? e.g., strip huge request_body or binary blobs after hot period but keep error.stack and key tags.

raj: yes — we can run an exporter filter that drops attributes post-ingest or a downstream transformer that stores a lightweight span copy for cold. Otel supports processors for that.

anya: important: dashboard queries (p99 latency by endpoint) rely on indexed fields. if we archive index entries we lose fast rollups. need to keep rollup tables or metrics derived from traces.

sylvia: suggested compromise: keep time-series rollups (agg counts, p50/p95/p99 dims) for 365d, traces themselves follow hot/cold lifecycle. console can query rollups to show historical trends and only fetch raw traces for recent windows.

max: that helps product metrics, but support folks still need raw traces sometimes beyond 30d. rehydration SLA could be: <30s for single trace, <5m for bulk (per 50 traces). Is that realistic?

raj: bulk rehydrate depends on cold storage. If we use compressed object store (S3 Glacier Deep Archive equv.), rehydrate is slow and expensive. Need an intermediate "warm" tier (cheaper S3 IA) for 60-90d window to meet <30s rehydrate for single trace.

anya: warm tier keeps costs manageable. rough numbers: keeping 60d in warm tier vs 90d hot reduces egress + storage by ~60%. rough engineering estimate from last calc: extra $8k/mo vs baseline.

max: can someone draft config syntax we can ship to ops? want something we can put in release notes and console.

raj: putting a draft retention policy YAML (example):

```yaml
trace_lifecycle:
  default_tiers:
    hot:
      ttl_days: 30
      store: "fast-ssd"
      indexed: true
      keep_attributes: ["service","span.kind","error","http.status_code","exception.stacktrace"]
    warm:
      ttl_days: 90
      store: "s3-ia"
      indexed: false
      keep_attributes: ["service","span.duration","http.status_code"]
    cold:
      ttl_days: 365
      store: "s3-archive"
      indexed: false
      keep_attributes: ["service","span.id"]
  overrides_by_service:
    billing-service:
      hot.ttl_days: 60
      warm.ttl_days: 180
```

sylvia: love the shape. we need explicit keys for export sampling and attribute scrubbing rules too. add `export_sampling_rate` and `post_ingest_scrub` blocks.

anya: also add audit/comply flag for traces that should never be purged (PII/legal holds). those go to private vault and count against enterprise billing.

max: good point. add `preserve_on_hold: true` for those traces with a case id. ops can run holds API.

migrations-bot: NOTE: when changing lifecycle rules, existing indices won't auto-move. migration plan required: temp dual-write to warm store for transition window.

raj: thanks bot. we'll need a backfill job to rehydrate & reindex older traces if we change indexed fields. that's non-trivial.

anya: UX: console should show per-service policy + effective retention and cost estimate. let users tweak per-service tier with defaults at org level.

max: action items: 1) raj + sylvia to prototype warm-tier rehydrate path (ETA 2w). 2) anya to write retention YAML + UI mockups (ETA 1w). 3) cost office to validate numbers (dunno who owns that) — tagging @finance.

sylvia: I'll start a simple proof: store compressed json blobs in s3-ia with a small index in our DB to find object key quickly. rehydrate path: fetch blob, decompress, hydrate cache. will measure latencies.

raj: for safety also add exporter-level attribute drop for heavy fields: `drop_attrs: ["request_body","response_body"]` to reduce storage at ingestion.

anya: one more ask: telemetry team wants sample rate metadata on traces so we can correct dashboards. add `sampling_info` preserved in warm/cold.

max: cool. let's reconvene next Wed after prototypes. thanks all. (reacted with :thumbsup:)

otel-bot: exporter health: last 1h error rate 0.2% (ok)

migrations-bot: NOTE: remember to schedule migration maintenance window when flipping defaults.

anya: adding meeting to calendar. "Trace lifecycle policy sync" 30m next Wed.

max: perfect. done.
